exposure: maternal 50-g glucose challenge test (GCT) results (low GCT results <= 81 mg/dL vs. non-low-GCT results 82-139 mg/dL)
outcome: neurodevelopmental delays in 3-year-old children (communication, gross motor, fine motor, problem-solving skills)
cohort: Children of 12,472 women who underwent a 50-g glucose challenge test between 14 and 27 weeks of gestation, extracted from 104,062 foetal records of the Japan Environment and Children's Study.
finding: Low maternal GCT results were associated with a significantly higher incidence of neurodevelopmental delays in offspring (particularly in communication, gross motor, fine motor, and problem-solving skills) at 3 years of age, with the association influenced by offspring sex as no significant increase was observed for female offspring.
